newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Lite-On says orders from IBM to double.
newsitem.headline: Lite-On says orders from IBM to double.

text.p: Taiwan's Lite-On Technology Corp said on Thursday it expected monthly computer monitor orders from its biggest client, IBM, would double in 1997 from 1996.

Lite-On, the world's fifth largest monitor maker, said IBM's decision in late 1996 to abandon monitor production meant that Lite-On's monthly order from the U.S. giant would likely rise to 80,000 sets by the end of 1997 from 40,000 sets in 1996.
"We are expecting an increase of orders coming from IBM this year," Tina Kuo, a Lite-On director, said by telephone.
"We are hoping to get around 80,000 sets by the end of the year, but the exact number obviously will fluctuate according to actual demand at that time," she said.
Kuo said Lite-On hoped to raise its overall monitor production to 4.5 million sets for 1997 from 3.3 million sets in 1996.
Lite-On has three monitor plants and is planning to complete three more by the end of 1997.
